description: Two-panel SEM secondary-electron fractograph group (Fig. 12) of Charpy/toughness specimens broken at -40°C, both imaged at fracture-surface scale with a black 20 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner of each panel. Panel (a) is the 12 h aged 1.07% Si specimen: it is dominated by large, flat, cleavage-like facets separated by sharp ledges; on several favorably oriented facets sets of fine, closely spaced parallel linear markings (slip traces) run along one or two directions, and a few small rounded dark holes/pores and patches of fine ridge tearing interrupt the facets. Panel (b) is the 12 h aged 1.56% Si specimen: the same transgranular cleavage-like facet morphology is present, but the facets are more heavily sub-divided by tearing ridges and stepped ledges, with larger areas of fine plasticity/tearing and a slightly more rugged relief. No composition, phase or crystallographic annotations, magnification value, or axis scales are printed in either panel. Taken together, the two panels argue that at -40°C both silicon levels of the aged Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.9C steel fail by transgranular cleavage-like fractograhy with slip traces, i.e. that the low-temperature brittle mode is insensitive in nature to the 1.07–1.56% Si variation.

observations.observation: Both panels are SEM fractographs of fracture surfaces and each carries a black 20 µm scale bar in its lower-right corner.
Panel (a) shows large flat cleavage-like facets bounded by sharp ledges, with sets of fine parallel linear slip traces on some favorably oriented facets.
Panel (a) also contains a few small rounded dark holes/pores and narrow regions of tearing ridges, indicating locally non-faceted separation.
Panel (b) displays the same faceted transgranular appearance but with a rougher relief, more stepped ledges and more extensive tearing-ridge/fine-tearing patches than (a).
Neither panel prints a magnification value, composition, phase label or crystallographic annotation; only the 20 µm scale bar is available as a size reference.
The caption identifies (a) as the 12 h aged 1.07% Si specimen and (b) as the 12 h aged 1.56% Si specimen, both broken at -40°C.
The caption states that these fracture surfaces show mostly transgranular cleavage-like fracture with slip traces noted on certain favorably oriented cleavage facets.
The citing text states the steel is Fe-30Mn-9Al-(1.07-1.56Si)-0.9C with low phosphorus (<0.003% P), aged at 530°C, with specimens aged 12 h.

The citing text reports that lowering the testing temperature to -40°C sharply reduced notch toughness and produced mainly brittle fracture, with increasing silicon lowering breaking energy by an average of 15 J for samples aged 12 h.

The citing text attributes the slip traces on cleavage facets to planar-slip/shear-band related tensile separation of {111} glide planes, a mechanism associated with κ-carbide precipitation during aging.

subfigures.description: SEM fractograph of the 12 h aged 1.07% Si specimen broken at -40°C, with a 20 µm scale bar. Large flat transgranular cleavage-like facets with fine parallel slip traces on favorably oriented facets, sharp inter-facet ledges, minor dark rounded pores and small tearing-ridge regions.

SEM fractograph of the 12 h aged 1.56% Si specimen broken at -40°C, with a 20 µm scale bar. Same cleavage-like faceted morphology but with more tearing ridges, stepped ledges and fine ductile-tearing patches between facets.
